intro.heading: Create your first window
intro.summary: Build an app that runs without a GPU. It opens a window, handles the close request, and releases resources before exiting.
create.heading: 1. Create Main.hx
create.paragraph: After installing LIMEN, open the Limen directory that contains README.md and the limen subdirectory. Create a my-window directory inside it. In a plain text editor, save the code as my-window/Main.hx. Check that the filename ends in .hx.
compile.heading: 2. Compile and run
compile.paragraph: Copy limen.hdll from the build output into my-window. If your Windows bundle includes hl.exe and libhl.dll, copy both files there too. On Linux and macOS, make sure HashLink is on your PATH and its system dependencies are installed.
compile.paragraph2: Save the following block as my-window/build.hxml. The -cp .. line adds the parent directory containing the LIMEN sources, and -hl main.hl sets the bytecode output file.
compile.run: Open a terminal in my-window. If you're using the bundled Windows runtime, use .\hl.exe main.hl as the second command.
compile.expected: A window titled Hello, LIMEN! should open. Close it using the close button. Change the title in Main.hx, run both commands again, and check the result. Next, build an app or a game.
how-it-works.heading: 3. Walk through the code
how-it-works.haxe: import brings a class name into scope. HashLink starts execution at Main.main(). A final variable cannot be reassigned, while a var variable can. The outer while loop keeps the app running, and the inner loop drains the event queue. When running becomes false, the program destroys the window and exits. See the Haxe manual for more.
